A.explanation: About $41 \text{ N}$ is the vertical component of the right-hand string, $T_2 \sin 20^{\circ}$, not $T_1$.

B.explanation: About $77 \text{ N}$ comes from using the wrong trig ratio, such as $120 \cos 50^{\circ}$ or swapping sine and cosine for the $70^{\circ}$ angle.

C.explanation: Resolving vertically gives $T_1 \sin 70^{\circ} + T_2 \sin 20^{\circ} = 120 \text{ N}$, which with horizontal balance gives $T_1 \approx 113 \text{ N}$.

D.explanation: About $128 \text{ N}$ comes from dividing by $\sin 70^{\circ}$ alone as $120 / \sin 70^{\circ}$, ignoring the upward component from the second string.

hints: Look at the dashed horizontal line at the knot: $T_1$ is at $70^{\circ}$ above it on the left, so its upward part is $T_1 \sin 70^{\circ}$ and its leftward part is $T_1 \cos 70^{\circ}$.

In equilibrium the upward components of the two strings must add to the $120 \text{ N}$ weight, while the leftward component of $T_1$ must equal the rightward component of the other string at $20^{\circ}$.
Eliminate the right-hand tension using the horizontal balance $T_1 \cos 70^{\circ} = T_2 \cos 20^{\circ}$, then solve the vertical equation for $T_1$.
walkthrough: Identify the geometry from the diagram. $T_1$ makes $70^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, the other tension $T_2$ makes $20^{\circ}$ with the horizontal, and the two strings are at $90^{\circ}$ to each other.
State the equilibrium rules at the knot. Resultant force is zero, so sum of vertical components $= 120 \text{ N}$ upward balance and sum of horizontal components $= 0$.
Write the component equations. Vertically: $T_1 \sin 70^{\circ} + T_2 \sin 20^{\circ} = 120 \text{ N}$. Horizontally: $T_1 \cos 70^{\circ} = T_2 \cos 20^{\circ}$.
Substitute to remove $T_2$. From horizontal balance, $T_2 = T_1 \cos 70^{\circ} / \cos 20^{\circ}$. Using $\cos 70^{\circ} \approx 0.342$ and $\cos 20^{\circ} \approx 0.940$, $T_2 \approx 0.364 T_1$.

Solve vertically. $T_1 \sin 70^{\circ} + (0.364 T_1)\sin 20^{\circ} = 120 \text{ N}$. With $\sin 70^{\circ} \approx 0.940$ and $\sin 20^{\circ} \approx 0.342$, this is $0.940 T_1 + 0.124 T_1 \approx 120 \text{ N}$.
Calculate $T_1 \approx 120 / 1.064 \approx 113 \text{ N}$ with unit $\text{N}$ as required for force. This is option C.
